statements.statement: Mid-level representations and closed-loop simulation testing are employed to facilitate training and deployment of autonomous driving models.
There remains a significant limitation due to error accumulation and distribution shift during closed-loop operation.
This limitation contributes to failures such as the model getting stuck or colliding with parked vehicles despite viable passing options.
Pure imitation learning approaches have been found insufficient even with large datasets and mid-level input/output representations.

Current methods do not adequately address these challenges, indicating a gap in effective strategies to mitigate error accumulation and distribution shift in closed-loop imitation learning for autonomous driving.
